text:
sam: Heads-up — after the Calico upgrade (v3.24 -> v3.26) last night we're seeing intermittent pod-to-pod packet loss and big east-west tail latency spikes on the inferencing fleet (gpu-pool-us-west2).

maria: saw the same. Model RPCs time out ~200-500ms extra p99, some retries. Affects inter-node traffic more but also some intra-node.

raj: I checked k8s events, a bunch of "NetworkUnreachable" and "Failed to create endpoint" for a few pods during the rollout. kube-proxy logs show conntrack churn.

sam: quick checks I ran:
- `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide` -> calico-node crashloop on a couple hosts during the upgrade window
- `ip link show` on node -> MTU on cali+eth0 is inconsistent (1500 vs 1450)
- `calicoctl node status` -> BGP up, but routes flapping on nodes with high packet loss

maria: Also ran tcpdump between two model pods: `tcpdump -i any host <pod-ip>` — saw lots of ICMP "frag needed" and retransmits. Tracepath from pod->pod shows MTU drop to 1400 on overlay hops.

raj: Sounds like encapsulation/MTU regression in the new calico dataplane. Did we enable IPIP/ENCAP changes? Change log mentions BPF dataplane adjustments.

sam: We rolled calico with default MTU calculation. New agent seems to mis-detect host NIC offloading and sets MTU too high for VXLAN. On hosts with RDMA NICs we saw kernel messages about GRO/TSO offload drops.

oncall: Infra-bot reported ~12% of pods in gpu-pool-us-west2 had transient network errors between 02:12-02:47 UTC. Linked metrics: packet_loss, tcp_retransmits, p999 latency.

maria: Immediate mitigation options? I'm thinking:
- roll back to v3.24 (fastest)
- force MTU override to 1450 in calico config and restart nodes
- disable BPF mode on a few canary nodes and switch to iptables backend to compare

raj: Rollback plan: helm rollback is available but need to coordinate drain of GPU nodes carefully (jobs running). Workaround we used last time: set FELIX_IPV6SUPPRESSION? (typo) — actually `FELIX_DEFAULTENDPOINTTOHOSTACTION=ACCEPT` not relevant. But setting `veth_mtu` override worked.

sam: Idea: patch DaemonSet to set env `NODENAME_MTU_OVERRIDE=1450` on 2 canary nodes and run connectivity tests before full rollback. That avoids large-scale drain.

maria: Agreed. Also enable `cni.ctrd` logs and capture `ethtool -k` for offload settings on the problematic hosts. I'm worried about RDMA-enabled hosts — might need kernel param tweaks.

raj: I'll spin up a test job: schedule two pods on same node and one across nodes, run iperf3 and ping, compare after forcing MTU. Will post results.

oncall: tagging @eng-sre oncall for visibility. If rollback is needed we should open a maintenance window and alert customers (some inference endpoints already retried).

sam: Thanks. If rollback is the path, let's prepare rollback doc with steps to: 1) cordon + drain eligibility for GPU nodes, 2) helm rollback to v3.24, 3) verify calico-node restart and `calicoctl status`, 4) run smoke pings and load test on model endpoints.

maria: Also record packet capture and `cilium`/`calico` metrics for postmortem (even if we rollback). We should file an issue with vendor including dmesg, kernel, MTU data.

raj: Update: iperf3 across nodes before MTU patch: bandwidth drops to ~400Mbps with lots of retransmits. After forcing 1450 on calico config on one canary node: bandwidth normalized and retransmits gone.

sam: Good. Let's proceed with canary MTU override on 3 hosts, monitor 30m, then escalate rollback if anything persists.

maria: Will prepare commands and playbook with exact helm values and `kubectl patch daemonset` snippet. Posting in #runbook when ready. :thumbsup:

oncall: Noted — alerting support to expect incoming tickets and adding status page note if rollback required.

sam: Thanks team. Keep updates here.
